p-nakedandfamousdenim-14679562813805.d:
The Sea Island Selvedge is a 12oz Japanese selvedge denim crafted from Virgin American Sea Island Cotton—the most luxurious denim we’ve ever produced. Sea Island Cotton is an ultra-rare Extra-Long Staple cotton. Renowned for its silky luster, uniform texture, cashmere-like softness, and exceptional durability, this cotton has a rich and storied past. Originally cultivated in the West Indies in the 1600s, it was once so coveted that British royalty tried to keep it exclusive. In the 1800s, seeds made their way to the American colonies, but a devastating beetle infestation nearly wiped it out in the 1920s.
Fast forward to 2015…. seeds that were tucked away in a seed vault are plated in Texas and New Mexico. This American-grown strain, genetically identical to the original variety, is now being used by select Japanese mills, including ours. Inspired by 1920s-era denim, this fabric offers a glimpse into an alternate history. What if Sea Island Cotton had become the standard? Imagine a world where silky-soft, ultra-durable jeans was the norm! Finishing details include contrast stitching, a durable paper patch, antique copper hardware, and a pink selvedge ID.

p-nakedandfamousdenim-8050660802718.d: The Frankenstein Denim is a 14oz Japanese denim, intricately woven in an alternating twill pattern. True to its name, this denim is a mishmash of various construction details. The weave pattern alternates every 2 inches between left-hand twill and right-hand twill throughout the fabric. Since this denim does not adhere to a single twill direction, it cannot undergo anti-skewing, a traditional finishing process designed to eliminate the natural twist of the fabric. Consequently, the sections of left-hand and right-hand twill will twist along their bias over time, enhancing the fabric’s dynamic texture. Crafted with big slub yarns that alternate between thick and thin sections, this denim not only offers an incredible texture but also affects dye penetration during the rope dyeing process. This results in sections of the yarn fading at different rates, revealing a stunning spectrum of indigo hues as the denim ages. In striving towards more eco-conscious production methods, one area we’re exploring is the use of recycled materials. The 7oz denim used here is woven from recycled cotton, reclaimed from offcuts and waste fabric, byproducts of the Japanese garment industry. Where ordinarily this textile waste would be incinerated, the fabrics are shredded before the fibres are re-spun into recycled cotton yarns. As the yarns produced comprise very fine fibres, once woven they result in a fabric that is softer, looser, and more pliable than our other denim at the equivalent weight, displaying a characterful neppy texture and appearance.

The armadillo buckle comes from a few different points of inspiration, based on certain elements of various buckles we have in our archive, all coming together to form this beaut. We developed our own custom mold with a partnering brass foundry here in the states, and churned out these solid brass buckles.
The armadillo holds a special place in our hearts because of its history in the music scene in Austin. Jim Franklin brought the armadillo to the forefront of pop-art and used it in a lot of the concert posters he made. As his art made its way into the psych-pop psych-rock scene, that psychedelic culture sort-of adopted the armadillo from Jim, and the folks behind the Vulcan Gas Company founded the Armadillo World Headquarters in the early 70s. The 'Dillo was where Willie Nelson first played to both hippies and rednecks, which was where Cosmic Country started.
This buckle means a lot to us, not just because it's an awesome piece, but because it really feels like a perfect representation of the inspiration behind the collection.
